ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 16555, as amended), especially Articles 5-2, 5-3, 5-5 and 5-7; Enforcement Decree of the same Act; Financial Services Commission Regulation on Customer Identification and Verification of Beneficial Owners; Commercial Act Articles 19, 20, 23, 24 and 25; Foreign Investment Promotion Act; Commercial Registration Act; and applicable FATF Recommendations incorporated by KoFIU supervisory guidance.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Certificate of Corporate Facts of each corporate UBO or parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry, chamber of commerce, or competent court in the UBO or parent home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For a document originating in a Hague Apostille Convention state: notarize the original before a notary if required, obtain a single apostille from the competent authority of the state of origin, and then present the apostilled document in South Korea; never add consular legalization. For a document originating in a non-Hague state: notarize the original if required, obtain consular legalization through the Republic of Korea Embassy or Consulate with territorial jurisdiction, including any Ministry of Foreign Affairs certification required in the document's origin country, and never apply an apostille. The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive. Korean-issued documents are apostilled by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Hague destinations and are consular legalized by the destination country's embassy for non-Hague destinations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Existence and Compliance of the parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies or domestic tax authority in the UBO or parent home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For a Hague-Apostille-state document: notarize only if the issuing authority requires it, then obtain an apostille from the designated competent authority; do not apply consular legalization. For a non-Hague-state document: notarize, then complete consular legalization through the Republic of Korea Embassy or Consulate responsible for the jurisdiction; do not apply an apostille. These authentication channels are mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution authorizing the incorporation of the Korean Yuhan Hoesa and appointing a registered representative, together with the Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors and corporate secretary of the parent company, with certification of resolution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If issued in a Hague Apostille Convention state: certify the board resolution and signature, then obtain an apostille from the competent state authority; no consular legalization may be added. If issued in a non-Hague state: certify the resolution before a notary and then obtain consular legalization from the Republic of Korea Embassy or Consulate; an apostille must not be applied. The apostille and consular legalization routes are parallel alternatives and shall not be layered.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Memorandum and Articles of Incorporation of the parent or UBO entity, including all amendments
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or authenticated copy issued by the parent entity's company secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Hague Convention origins: produce a certified true copy, notarize if required, then have the certified copy apostilled by the origin country's apostille authority; no consular legalization thereafter. For non-Hague origins: notarize, then obtain legalization from the Republic of Korea Embassy or Consulate covering the jurisdiction and any required foreign ministry certification; no apostille may be used. The two legalization paths are mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the UBO or parent relationship bank addressed to the future Korean corporate bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Deposit-taking financial institution in the UBO or parent home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Hague Convention jurisdictions: have the bank sign the letter, notarize the authorized signatory if required, then arrange an apostille from the designated competent authority; do not apply consular legalization. For non-Hague jurisdictions: notarize the bank officer's signature and then obtain consular legalization from the Republic of Korea Embassy or Consulate with jurisdiction; do not apply an apostille. Apostille and consular legalization must never be combined in one chain.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before any filing, every UBO, director, officer, signatory and agent must be screened against the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit designation database, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU and UK consolidated lists, and the domestic sanctions list of the Republic of Korea. For all individuals and entities, include PEP status checks covering foreign, domestic and international organisation PEPs, their family members and close associates; use independent databases and registry records to verify identity; capture the source of wealth and source of funds for any PEP or higher-risk connection; perform adverse media checks and negative news screening; refresh the screening at account opening, at any beneficial-ownership change, and on a rolling 365-day basis; document every hit in an escalation memo and obtain senior management approval before proceeding.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: IREOS - Internet Registration Office operated by the Supreme Court of Korea, Commercial Registration module for company name search and clearance; supplemented by the Commercial Registration Information Search portal of the Korean court registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered trade name of a Yuhan Hoesa must be expressed in Hangul in the court registry; a romanized Latin-alphabet equivalent is permitted for banking, tax invoice and English contract use, but the primary registered name must be in Hangul and must include the legal-form suffix Yuhan Hoesa or an equivalent statutory transliteration. incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Korean Commercial Act, Chapter VII (Limited Liability Company / Yuhan Hoesa), Articles 287-2 through 287-97, together with the Commercial Registration Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act for non-resident equity participation
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Office, Civil Division, the Seoul Central District Court or the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the company's registered office
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Commercial Registration Application Form for Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company, annexed to the notarized Articles of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Yuhan Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act. The incorporators may fix initial capital at any amount above zero in the Articles of Incorporation. If a foreign investor participates, the equity contribution must be reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and documentary proof of remittance must be retained; however, no blocked escrow account is legally required. Bank-held subscription funds may not be disbursed until commercial registration is effected.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION BY WRITTEN CONSENT OF THE DIRECTORS AND FOUNDING MEMBERS OF YUHAN HOESA, A KOREAN LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY, DULY ADOPTED AS THE FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION. IN ACCORDANCE with Articles 287-2, 287-3, 287-34, 287-37, 287-38 and 287-58 of the Korean Commercial Act, and by the unanimous written consent of the directors and founding members, it is ordered and resolved as follows. 1. SUBSCRIPTION AND CONTRIBUTION OF SHARE CAPITAL. The initial share capital of the company shall be KRW 60,000,000 divided into 60,000 contributed units of KRW 1,000 each. Each founding member subscribes in writing to the exact number of units set out in the capital ledger. Every contribution shall be paid in full in cash into an interest-bearing capital deposit account opened in the name of the company before incorporation, and the bank deposit certificate shall be preserved in the corporate minute book. No founder or director may withdraw, assign, pledge, or encumber any contributed funds prior to the completion of the official commercial registration, except as expressly authorized by Korean law. 2. ADOPTION AND DESIGNATION OF THE REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office and principal place of business of the company shall be established at 123 Teheran-ro, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, 06136, Republic of Korea. The Representative Director is authorized to execute, amend, and terminate the office lease and all connected utility, communication, and service contracts, and to file the registered address with the competent District Court Registration Office and the National Tax Service. 3. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. Effective upon the submission of incorporation registration, the following officers are duly appointed to the offices appearing beside their names: the Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer, the Director of Corporate Affairs, the Financial Director, and the Compliance Officer. The Compliance Officer shall supervise anti-money laundering controls, personal information protection obligations, and internal governance policies. Each appointed officer accepts his or her office and irrevocably covenants to act with fiduciary care and in full compliance with Korean corporate, commercial, tax, and regulatory law. 4. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The company shall open, maintain, and close such deposit, settlement, wire transfer, foreign currency, and securities accounts as may be required with any commercial bank licensed to operate in the Republic of Korea. All checks, negotiable instruments, wire transfers, and bank mandates shall be valid when signed by the Representative Director and the Financial Director jointly, except that a single signature by the Representative Director shall be sufficient for transactions not exceeding KRW 10,000,000. 5. GOVERNANCE, ACCOUNTING, AND AUDIT. The company shall maintain proper financial books, statutory registers, and records. The Financial Director is directed to open or appoint an independent examiner if required by asset thresholds. 6. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION AND EFFECTIVENESS. Each statutory officer is authorized to execute all necessary documents, to file all permits, tax registrations, and regulatory statements, and to represent the company before courts, banks, and public authorities. This First Board Resolution is irrevocable as to capital subscription and shall continue in force until amended or revoked by a subsequent lawful members' resolution. THE FOREGOING RESOLUTION IS HEREBY AUTHORIZED, ADOPTED, AND RECORDED AS THE FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE COMPANY. END OF RESOLUTION.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Notary Public commissioned by the Ministry of Justice, acting under the Notary Public Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founding members or their authorized counsel shall draft the Articles of Incorporation of the Yuhan Hoesa with the exact corporate name, corporate purpose, registered office street address, initial capital schedule, unit contribution rights, and governance provisions. The founders must execute the articles individually or by proxy; execution must be in the presence of a Korean notary who verifies identity, legal capacity, and legality of the business purpose. The notary shall issue a notarized original and copies, which are mandatory annexes to the court filing. Foreign founders must present apostilled or consular-verified passports and identification, and any corporate founder must present certified constitutional documents. This step is a legal precondition; the Articles must be stamped by the notary before any later capital deposits or registration filings.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation
Government-issued passport or national identity card of each founder
Power of attorney if executed by proxy
Proof of address and nationality of each founder
Capital contribution schedule and unit allocation ledger
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary objects, the founders must cure the defective clauses by amending the draft articles and re-executing them before another notary, provide compliant apostilled identification documents, or substitute an authorized Korean counsel to correct formal errors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Contribution and Issuance of Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank licensed in the Republic of Korea, including major domestic banks and foreign bank branches with corporate banking authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After opening a temporary corporate contribution account in the company's name, each founding member must remit the full value of subscribed units by wire transfer or cash deposit. The bank shall verify the beneficial owner, apply customer due diligence under the Financial Action Task Force standards and Korean anti-money laundering rules, and then issue a deposit certificate confirming the amount, account title, date, and currency of deposit. The deposit certificate must be submitted to the Registration Court to prove capital payment. This certificate must contain the corporate name as stated in the Articles, and the funds remain restricted until commercial registration is achieved. For foreign investors, the remittance must be traceable through bank records and acceptable as foreign investment under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Corporate account application and bank onboarding forms
Wire transfer instructions and source-of-funds evidence
Passport of the authorized signatories
Founders' taxpayer identification numbers or passports for AML,
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays or rejects the opening certificate, the founders should supplement the source-of-funds documents, correct beneficial ownership declarations, or open the account at a different licensed bank; any suspicious transaction report must be resolved through formal documentation with the bank's compliance officer.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Incorporation Registration Filing with the District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Office of the Seoul Central District Court or the District Court having jurisdiction over the location of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The representative director or a licensed Korean attorney shall file the Commercial Registration Application Form with the court's commercial registration section. The application must attach the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the bank capital deposit certificate, written appointments and signed acceptances by the statutory officers, proof of ownership or consent to the registered office, and the prescribed corporate seal report. The registering judge shall examine whether the statutory requirements are satisfied, confirm that all directors and the auditor have not been disqualified, and verify that the business purpose is lawful. Upon approval, the court records the company in the commercial register and issues a certified extract of incorporation. Registration is a constitutive act; the legal existence of the company begins at the time of the court's entry.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration Application Form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital deposit certificate issued by the bank
Written acceptance letters of directors and auditor
Landlord's consent or lease agreement for the registered office
Corporate seal specimen and seal registration report
Identity documents of all statutory officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registering judge issues a corrective order, submit the missing exhibits within the prescribed period, amend the Articles where necessary, or file a supplementary registration petition. If the registration is refused, the applicant may appeal such refusal to the court within two weeks.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, E-Commerce Disclosure, and Foreign Investment Post-Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service through the HomeTax system, local municipal revenue office, and KOTRA Invest Korea for foreign-invested enterprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after the court issue the certificate of incorporation, the company must apply for a business registration certificate with the local district tax office under the Value Added Tax Act. The company shall also register for corporate income tax withholding, complete the electronic commerce consumer information disclosure requirements under the Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce, and, if the shareholder is a non-resident, report the foreign investment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act through KOTRA or the designated receiving bank. The company must obtain the Foreign Investment Enterprise Certificate where applicable. Any future mobile or on-premise retail activities shall require a supplementary business registration notice. Standard corporate books and bank signature cards are also activated during this phase.
required_dossiers: Court-issued certificate of incorporation
Registered corporate seal certificate
Notarized Articles of Incorporation and court extract
Office lease contract or ownership certificate
Bank account verification and deposit certificate
Foreign investment report form and remittance certificate if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office or KOTRA issues a query or suspension, the company should correct clerical discrepancies, clarify the ownership percentage, produce verified bank remittance records, and, where required, file a formal administrative objection within the statutory appeal period printed in the notice.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing operation is triggered under ISIC 4791 electronic catalog retail of industrial MRO supplies
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - a general business registration under the Value Added Tax Act and an online e-commerce consumer disclosure filing are sufficient; no special industrial operating license is required

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - the Ministry of Environment would only become competent if a future warehouse or logistics facility is developed
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - ISIC 4791 is retail via electronic catalogue and is not classified among the EIA project categories requiring full Environmental Impact Assessment or simplified Environmental Registration
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the company does not operate a stationary pollution source, discharge process wastewater, emit volatile organic compounds, or generate hazardous industrial waste at incorporation stage; future logistics sites must be assessed under the Clean Air Conservation Act and Water Environment Conservation Act before construction

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable at initial formation. If the company later operates a warehouse or physical showroom, it must obtain the Civil Defense fire safety completion inspection and an occupational safety and health compliance certificate under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, together with structural load inspection for any storage rack system exceeding legal thresholds.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, electronic portal HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity without a fixed place of business in Korea must appoint a domestic tax representative before any VAT registration. The representation agreement and a power of attorney must be submitted to the NTS district tax office that has jurisdiction over the tax representative. The foreign entity must file the Application for Business Registration (Sa-roe-p-ja-deung-rok) together with certified copies of the entity's Articles of Incorporation, the Certificate of Foreign Business Registration or equivalent incorporation evidence from the home country, a notarized copy of the foreign entity's corporation certificate, identification of the entity's representatives, and the domestic tax representative's appointment documents. If the entity establishes a Korean place of business (including a fixed facility used for e-commerce storage or logistics), it must register with the district tax office covering that place of business within 20 days of commencement. For the Yuhan Hoesa LLC, which is a Korean domestic legal entity, the standard procedure applies: the company must complete business registration at the local NTS district tax office after company registration, and the NTS will issue a 10-digit Business Registration Number (TIN/VAT ID) within several working days. A foreign non-resident seller of digital or e-commerce services without a fixed place of business must still obtain a VAT registration number through a tax representative and must report supply of services subject to Korean VAT, including via the HomeTax portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None under Korean tax law. A Yuhan Hoesa is statutorily treated as a domestic corporation for Korean corporate and VAT purposes and has no check-the-box or pass-through election. A wholly-owned Korean subsidiary of a domestic corporate group may elect consolidated corporate tax filing under the Framework Act on Corporate Taxation if all qualifying subsidiaries consent, but this affects income tax, not indirect tax. Hybrid mismatch elections are not available domestically; only treaty-based tie-breaker arguments may apply, and these are not registration elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: All resident business entities are required to register for VAT before commencement of business. A simplified taxpayer with annual taxable turnover below KRW 80,000,000 may use simplified filing, but there is no exemption from registration for a domestic LLC. Foreign non-resident suppliers supplying goods or services in Korea or electronic services to Korean customers are subject to mandatory VAT registration without any turnover threshold; a tax representative is required. Thus, the only operative threshold for practical simplified registration is KRW 80,000,000 annual turnover, which does not defer registration for a limited liability company formed as a Yuhan Hoesa.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered Korean businesses, including Yuhan Hoesa LLCs, must issue electronic tax invoices (e-tax invoices) for supplies to other VAT-registered businesses. E-tax invoices must be transmitted to the National Tax Service through the HomeTax real-time clearance system by the day after the date of issuance. The NTS assigns a unique tax invoice number and validates the invoice in its central system. For B2C supplies, cash receipts must be issued and reported through HomeTax if the customer requests them or if the transaction is paid by credit card. The Korean e-tax invoice system is mandatory regardless of sector, and there is no alternative paper-based clearance for VAT-registered entities; non-compliance triggers procedural penalties under the Value-Added Tax Act and the Framework Act on National Taxes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under Article 24 of the Korean Value-Added Tax Act for the export of goods when the goods are physically moved out of Korea and the export declaration is accepted by Korean Customs, for the supply of services rendered to foreign persons for use outside Korea, and for the supply of goods or services incidental to international maritime or air transport. For the B2B e-commerce MRO catalog model, zero-rating can be applied to supplies of tangible MRO hardware sold to customers outside Korea, provided the export declaration is made and the products are delivered through an export process; digital services (if any) supplied to non-Korean B2B customers for use outside Korea may also qualify if the place of supply is properly substantiated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Bill of Entry or reference number as accepted by Korea Customs Service)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing international carriage
Commercial invoice and packing list describing the shipped MRO items
Foreign Exchange Trading Certificate or Inward Remittance Advice issued by a foreign exchange bank evidencing receipt of export proceeds in an eligible currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Korean Customs and the National Tax Service closely scrutinize export zero-rating claims. The spatial movement of goods must be corroborated by the full export documentation bundle, and the exporter must maintain records of the transaction, including the customs export declaration, B/L, commercial invoice, packing list, and evidence of foreign exchange receipt. If the NTS determines that a zero-rated export was not actually exported or that documentation is false, it will assess the 10% VAT retroactively and impose an additional penalty of up to 40% of the unpaid tax for deliberate evasion, together with penalties for false or omitted tax invoices and a negligence surcharge of 10% for incomplete substantiation; the taxpayer is also liable for interest for late payment. Willful submission of forged export evidence constitutes criminal tax fraud under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and may result in up to three years imprisonment or a fine. The NTS also has a five-year statutory audit window (ten years for tax fraud or reasonable cause to suspect intentional concealment) for restoring excluded zero-rated supplies.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) alongside the Ministry of Strategy and Finance (MOSF) as the coordinating Foreign Exchange Administration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a largely convertible foreign exchange regime, with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA) providing for market-determined exchange rates and generally unrestricted current-account convertibility. The Korean won (KRW) is freely usable for trade and service transactions, and the Bank of Korea intervenes only under exceptional one-way volatility conditions to smooth disorderly market movements. Capital-account transactions, including inbound foreign direct investment (FDI), are also legally permitted but are subject to mandatory reporting and declaration mechanisms administered by the Ministry of Strategy and Finance and delegated to foreign exchange banks. Surrender requirements for export proceeds are not based on a statutory conversion ratio; rather, exporters are required to receive export settlement proceeds within a defined period and may hold such proceeds in designated foreign currency accounts. Profit remittance by a Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) is legally permissible once the foreign-invested entity has filed the annual foreign exchange report and fulfilled corporate income tax and withholding tax obligations. Practical hurdles to dividend remittance include documentary demands for certified financial statements, tax clearance certificates, and proof of the original capital injection through the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA) notification track. Overall, current-account profits are freely repatriable, but capital-account movements require impeccable paper trails and adherence to reporting timelines to avoid penalties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters must receive export proceeds within 180 days from the date of export clearance, extendable through prior approval from the foreign exchange bank for justified operational reasons. No mandatory loan is made up to a fixed percentage of export receipts; instead, the proceeds may be deposited into a foreign currency account at a tier-1 domestic bank, and the exporter must present the underlying export customs declaration (Sinyoung and KCS movement) plus the export bill of lading to support the receipt and exemption from immediate conversion.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Foreign Currency Deposit) and Basic Operational KRW Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech EMIs (e.g., Revolut, Qonto, Airwallex) have low viability and material legal constraints for serving a Korean legal entity. Under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act and FETA, an authorized foreign exchange bank must be a licensed financial institution in Korea; offshore EMIs generally do not hold a Korean banking license and cannot provide local IBAN-like account rails for KRW clearing. In addition, KYC requirements mandate presence of the company's signatory in Korea, and banks are liable for identity verification. An overseas EMI cannot perform the required in-branch identification and foreign investment notification. Therefore, use of offshore EMIs is limited to ancillary payment collection via card acquiring or trade settlement facilitation through partners, but they are not acceptable as the primary corporate treasury account provider.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory directors of the Korean LLC must appear physically at a designated domestic branch of the chosen tier-1 bank for the initial onboarding interview, presenting passport, corporate seals, and apostilled/certified constitutional documents. A remote consular proxy opening is not generally recognized; Korea's non-face-to-face account opening process does not extend to foreign-invested corporate entities. The bank will insist on an in-branch meeting with the signatory director and, in the case of beneficial-owner complexity, also require the ultimate beneficial owner's verified identification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity if the Korean LLC is owned by a corporate chain outside Korea
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Aggregated corporate structure chart to the ultimate beneficial owner, registered certificates and good-standing certificates along the ownership chain, passport copies of all beneficial owners who own or control more than 25%, and a board resolution directing the LLC to file the beneficial ownership declaration with the Financial Action Task Force-aligned Korean FIU.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability to authenticate the source of initial share capital for the capital escrow account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements of the investing parent (or private wealth documentation for individual investors), six months of bank statements proving origin of the remittance, a sworn source-of-funds declaration via a certified translation, and, if funded by intercompany loan, a formal loan agreement with interest-rate terms and adequate solvency evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based ML red flags from cross-border e-commerce MRO product flows with low-priced industrial hardware
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed product catalogue with unit price benchmarks, representative purchase invoices, supplier contracts, bills of lading / airway bills, customs declarations, proof of actual warehousing or freight forwarding arrangements, and a documented mark-to-market valuation of affected inventory to demonstrate commercial realism.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions screening hit on foreign suppliers or downstream receivers of MRO supplies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed name-screening and risk-scoring report from a reputable trade compliance vendor, exclusion certificates from suppliers, end-user attestations, applicable export-control licenses, and a narrative explanation from the compliance officer addressing the nature of goods, end-use, and counterparty jurisdiction.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital must be routed through a domestic foreign exchange bank using the SWIFT MT103 protocol, with the remitting institution including the designated FD (Foreign Direct Investment) notification number in the payment narrative. The funds are credited to the Yuhan Hoesa's foreign currency capital escrow account, then converted to KRW at the daily benchmark rate. Under FIPA, the foreign investor must file an FDI notification with the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy or delegated bank prior to remittance; the bank issues an Investment Verification Certificate (Certificate of Foreign-Exchange Bank Having Performed the Notification) on receipt. The monetary authority comparison among the returned message and export/import customs declarations is used for capital verification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for industrial MRO import settlements should utilise (a) SWIFT MT103 for open-account and small-value payments where the supplier accepts normal transfer latency; (b) Commercial Letters of Credit (L/Cs) for high-value or risky procurements, where the L/C is issued from the Korean corporate bank and conforming documents are presented before payment; and (c) Documentary Collections (D/P or D/A) as an intermediate cost-reduction mechanism, especially for routine repeat distributions of standard MRO components.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Covered KRW/USD forward contracts backed by explicit commercial underlying exposure (trade payables or forecasted export receivable amounts with signed purchase orders) and executed with a licensed onshore bank

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on KRW/USD allowed for eligible trade and structural hedging transactions, with onshore and offshore counterparties subject to FETA reporting and a prohibition on speculative booking

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for long-term capital-account hedges, convertible to legacy MT330/MT340 messaging, subject to notification to the designated foreign exchange bank and MOSF threshold declarations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary General Meeting of Members, Approval of Financial Statements and Settlement of Accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the Yuhan Hoesa; for externally audited companies, the audited accounts and business report are additionally held by the Financial Supervisory Service through the DART electronic disclosure system.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year end, no later than March 31 of the following year; the next business day applies if the statutory date falls on a weekend or public holiday.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No automatic registry fee is imposed, but failure to approve settlement accounts blocks the timely corporate tax filing and exposes the company to a 20 percent unfiled-return additional tax; a member may seek a court order for convening the meeting, and persistent non-filing of a closed annual account together with tax delinquency can lead to business registration cancellation and administrative strike-off by the competent Korean registry and tax authorities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax and Local Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service through Hometax for national corporate income tax and the competent si, gun, or gu local government for the local income tax surcharge.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 of the following year for a December 31 fiscal year; for a non-December fiscal year, within three months of the fiscal year end; the return must be accompanied by the externally audited or internally certified financial statements as applicable.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An unfiled or late-filed return triggers an additional tax of 20 percent of the payable corporate income tax; underreported tax attracts an understatement penalty of 10 percent or 40 percent for false tax base, plus daily overdue interest of 0.022 percent; continued failure to file tax returns for repeated years may result in business registration cancellation and a court-registry administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Periodic Returns for the Industrial MRO E-Commerce Supply Business
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half calendar period return is due July 25; second half calendar period return is due January 25; corporate taxpayers also file quarterly preliminary VAT returns by April 25 and October 25.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted VAT returns attract up to 30 percent additional tax on unreported output tax and 0.022 percent per-day interest on unpaid VAT; failure to issue correct electronic tax invoices incurs penalties from 2 percent to 5 percent of supply value; repeated non-filing can lead to revocation of the business registration and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Compulsory External Audit Report Filing with the Financial Supervisory Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service through DART; the audit must be performed by a certified Korean CPA registered with the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a company subject to mandatory audit, the external audit report on annual financial statements must be delivered in time for the ordinary general meeting, and the electronic audit report and business report must be filed through DART within the period prescribed by the Act on External Audit of Corporations, normally within one month after the ordinary general meeting and in any event before the final corporate tax return due date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission of a required statutory audit exposes the company and its responsible directors to administrative fines up to KRW 50 million and renders the annual financial statements invalid for tax purposes, triggering the same 20 percent unfiled-return penalty and adverse auditor designation by the Financial Supervisory Service; continuous violation combined with overdue returns can lead to business registration cancellation and judicial strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Annual Report and Beneficial Ownership Change Notification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency and the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The annual report must be submitted within 30 days after the end of the fiscal year; any transfer of a foreign shareholder interest, change of actual controlling shareholder, or change in foreign investment ratio must be reported within 30 days of the event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or a false annual report gives rise to administrative fines up to KRW 2 million; non-reporting may result in revocation of foreign-invested enterprise status, loss of statutory protections and tax incentives, and possible re-characterization of profit remittances as non-deductible dividends.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Register Audit, Member Register Update and Registered Agent Compliance Certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate secretary, registered agent, directors, and the members of the Yuhan Hoesa; no government filing fee applies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The register audit must be completed before the ordinary general meeting, in all cases no later than March 31 for a December 31 year-end; any member transfer discovered during the year must be posted in the register of members within 30 days of the transfer and confirmed in the annual register audit.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Korean Commercial Act, a member transfer not recorded in the statutory register of members is ineffective against the Yuhan Hoesa; mismanaged registers can lead to director fines, personal liability to third parties, delayed share register rectification suits, and, in aggravated fraud cases, the administrative strike-off of the entity.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent certified CPA audit is mandated under the Korean Act on External Audit of Corporations if the Yuhan Hoesa has, at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year, total assets of KRW 12 billion or more, annual turnover or gross revenue of KRW 10 billion or more, or an annual average headcount of 100 or more full-time employees; a mandatory audit is also triggered where consolidated assets, revenue, or headcount exceed these thresholds, where the company is designated as a public-interest or financial-services-related company, or where a creditor, court, or qualifying shareholder holding 3 percent or more has validly required an auditor appointment. The primary asset threshold is approximately USD 9.2 million; the turnover equivalent is approximately USD 7.7 million.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) applies to public-interest and consolidated reporting groups; a non-listed Yuhan Hoesa may instead apply Korean GAAP (K-GAAP) and the SME simplified accounting standards approved by the Korean Accounting Standards Board; all statutory accounts must be presented in Korean won, and if K-GAAP is used for an exempt SME the statements must still comply with the Commercial Act and Act on External Audit of Corporations; the independent auditor must be licensed and registered in Korea.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korean law does not impose a separate stand-alone ultimate beneficial owner filing at the company registry for a private Yuhan Hoesa, but the Foreign-Invested Enterprise Annual Report to KOTRA and the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy functions as the annual UBO confirmation: every foreign-invested enterprise must confirm the identity, nationality, shareholding percentage, and ultimate beneficial ownership position within 30 days of fiscal year end; any transfer of a foreign participant's interest, any change of actual owner, or any shareholding transfer exceeding the statutory reporting threshold must also be reported within 30 days of the transaction and simultaneously posted to the statutory register of members before such transfer is effective against the company.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 to USD 1,500 per year for a registered office in Seoul or Incheon plus a licensed corporate secretarial agent covering annual filings, statutory register maintenance, and regulatory correspondence.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 to USD 12,000 for a below-threshold Yuhan Hoesa with limited B2B MRO transactions; USD 15,000 to USD 45,000 for a compulsory K-IFRS statutory audit and any consolidated group audit work.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national marginal rate; 26.4% combined headline rate when adding the 10% local income tax surcharge (progressive national tariffs: 9% for taxable income up to KRW 200m, 19% for KRW 200m-KRW 20bn, 21% for KRW 20bn-KRW 300bn, 24% above KRW 300bn)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Foreign direct investment in Tax-Free or Free Economic Zones may obtain a 100% national CIT exemption for 5 years and 50% reduction for the following 2 years under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act; R&D expenditure gives a statutory credit of up to 50%; technology-transfer gains, MRO catalog e-commerce in designated high-tech free zones, and small/medium enterprise progressive brackets reduce effective burden.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: NTS Form 6 - Foreign Corporation Corporate Income Tax Return filed by the domestic place of business through the HomeTax electronic filing portal (www.hometax.go.kr); the return is filed by the branch manager or appointed tax agent using the branch's Korean registration number.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing, with quarterly estimated corporate tax prepayments for branches with previous-year taxable income exceeding KRW 10 million.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The final corporate income tax return must be filed within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year (e.g., for a December 31 year-end, the due date is March 31 of the following calendar year); a one-month extension may be claimed if the foreign parent company's accounting records are closed abroad after the Korean deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1a - Corporate Identity and Branch Registration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Korean business registration number, foreign corporation name, head office address, domestic place of business address, representative director, and the closing date of foreign corporation's fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact registration number issued to the Korean branch by the local tax office. A foreign e-commerce seller that merely has a warehouse, local delivery agent, or dependent agent in Korea may be deemed to have a permanent establishment under Article 94 of the Corporate Tax Act and must file; if no PE exists, the non-resident should instead be covered by the simplified withholding return on Korean-source self-assessed income, not by Form 6.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5a - Taxable Period / Fiscal Year-Opening and Closing Dates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Beginning and ending dates of the 12-month taxable period; branch closure, liquidation, and change of accounting period events.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The taxable period normally follows the foreign parent's audited fiscal year, but when the Korean PE keeps separate books, the Korean branch may select a fiscal year that ends in the same calendar year. If the business starts after January 1, file the first short-period return within 3 months of commencement; misalignment of periods is a common trigger for PE attribution audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 12 - Taxable Base / Korean-Source Business Income Attributable to the PE
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit of the Korean PE after statutory adjustments: sales of industrial MRO hardware through the Korean catalog e-commerce site, inventory procurement, logistics, warehousing, and customer-support income pool.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the attributable income principle under the OECD authorized OECD approach codified by Korean tax jurisprudence; only expenses directly or reasonably allocated to the PE are deductible. Invoicing by the foreign head office or related supplier without local substance will be adjusted under Article 14 and Article 16 of the International Tax Adjustment Act, and the NTS may apportion profit by reference to capital, payroll, and sales in Korea.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 18 - Tax Adjustments / Non-Deductible Items and Exemptions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation from accounting net income to taxable income, including add-backs (e.g., non-deductible entertainment expense excess, punitive damages, deemed CFC income) and deductions (e.g., carried-forward losses, tax credits).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For imports of MRO products, transfer pricing adjustments must be reflected in this schedule; management fees paid to a foreign headquarters that are not supported by service documentation are non-deductible; treaty rate claims are not an adjustment here but must be evidenced in the withholding application schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 27 - Tax Credits / Foreign Tax Credit and DTA Reduction
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit for taxes imposed by foreign jurisdictions, plus withholding taxes already collected on Korean-source dividends, interest, or royalties; carryforward foreign tax credit schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean PE may credit foreign tax paid on income that Korea also taxes, up to the Korean tax attributable to the foreign income. No credit is allowed for taxes avoided through an offshore shell. To invoke a reduction of the final tax, attach the Tax Residency Certificate, a beneficial ownership declaration, and the withholding tax treaty rate application form; if the low-tax jurisdiction is not a recognized treaty partner, the credit is denied and an additional 20% plus 2% local resident surcharge is withheld.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of each related party, country code for head office, transaction type, invoice amount, intercompany payment terms, arm's length method used, and the local file/master file index.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All sales of industrial MRO supplies to/from related distributors, payment of catalog platform fees, logistics commissions, and shared service cost allocations must be individually itemized. If the aggregate cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 30 billion in the preceding fiscal year, the Local File and Master File are mandatory; failure to submit subjects the taxpayer to penalties and a 20% reassessment surcharge on the transfer pricing adjustment amount.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 6 triggers a 20% surcharge of the declared tax under Article 47-4 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, plus an overdue daily surcharge of 0.022% (up to 9.4%); an omission that exceeds 30% of the correct tax triggers a 40% penalty; gross fraudulent evasion above KRW 500 million becomes a criminal tax fraud referral under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and the Act on Aggravated Punishment of Specific Economic Crimes, with imprisonment and disqualification of directors; foreign directors can be placed on an NTS/JSOC blacklist restricting entry and exit.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% combined statutory withholding rate on outbound dividends paid by a Korean entity or branch to a non-resident corporation (20% national corporate withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge); a DTA may reduce the rate to 5-15%, normally 10% for a direct investor holding at least 10% and 15% otherwise in most Korean treaties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must first obtain and submit a Tax Residency Certificate from the tax authority of its state of residence, demonstrate through authentic documents that the recipient is the beneficial owner of the dividend, interest, or royalty (no back-to-back arrangement or conduit obligation to pay on the same income), and file with the Korean withholding agent before the payment date an application for the treaty rate using the NTS treaty-exemption/reduction application (with any required apostille or consular legalization). The withholding agent must attach this application to the monthly withholding return made through HomeTax by the 10th day of the following month; where the claim is after the withholding, the non-resident may apply for a refund through a corrective return within 3 years, but penalties are imposed unless the procedural requirement was met in good faith.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on cross-border royalties and interest is also 22% combined (20% national plus 2% local surcharge). Under most Korean income tax treaties, interest on arm's length intercompany loans is reduced to 10%, industrial patent and similar royalties to 5-10%, and software/MRO catalog platform licence royalties to 10%; the treaty rate is conditional on beneficial ownership, arm's length loan terms, and the absence of profit-seeking recharacterization of the interest payment. Where interest is paid by a Korean branch to a foreign head office or related lender, the interest may be non-deductible if the branch is thinly capitalized under Article 50 of the International Tax Adjustment Act.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The mandatory Local File threshold is annual cross-border related-party transactions of at least KRW 30 billion (roughly USD 22 million); the Master File is additionally mandatory for a multinational group whose consolidated Korean revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion and whose cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 30 billion, with the same trigger applying to the preceding business year; the Korean branch of the foreign MRO catalogue business must prepare contemporaneous documentation even below the threshold if the transaction amount is in a high-risk category.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not maintain a named Economic Substance Regulation regime like the UAE, but the economic substance doctrine is fully embedded in Korean tax law: Article 4 of the International Tax Adjustment Act authorizes the NTS to disregard substanceless transactions, Article 18 imposes CFC tax on base-company income that lacks real business activity, and the OECD authorized OECD approach is used for permanent establishment attribution. The MRO catalog e-commerce vehicle must demonstrate in Korea core income-generating activities (CIGA): local management, local warehousing/fulfilment, order-taking systems, credit-risk bearing, supplier contracts, and back-office staff. A Korean distribution entity with no Korean employees or business premises is a red flag and will be treated as having a Korean permanent establishment whose attributable profit and non-resident tax cannot be eliminated by re-domiciling the contract to a Hong Kong or Singapore shell.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Corporate Income Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately misstating the Korean taxable base by booking Korean B2B industrial MRO catalogue sales to the foreign parent in an undiscounted intra-group commission scheme, manufacturing fake intercompany invoices, or concealing the Korean fixed place of business through the Yuhan Hoesa letterhead while management is in fact directed from outside Korea.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act imposes imprisonment of up to 2 years and/or fines up to 3 times the evaded tax; Article 4 of the Framework Act on National Taxes and Article 47-3 impose a 40% erroneous-report penalty and daily overdue surcharge; once the amount evaded exceeds KRW 500 million, Article 3 of the Act on Aggravated Punishment of Specific Economic Crimes raises the imprisonment range to 3-20 years with a fine of 2-5 times the economic profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The Korean courts have consistently allowed piercing of the corporate veil when the entity is used to avoid taxes and separate the property rights of shareholders; directors may be jointly and severally assessed for the unpaid corporate tax, restitution and civil damages; a director convicted of tax fraud faces personal imprisonment, disqualification from serving as a director, seizure of personal bank accounts and shares, and a Ministry of Justice departure restriction/blacklist that bars exit from Korea until the tax and penalties are paid.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance and DTA Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing KR_YUHANGHOESA as a shell Korean LLC with a virtual office only, no full-time employees, no material local management, no Korean bank account in substance, and using a tax haven or treaty-state intermediary to route MRO sales income and claim a foreign tax credit or reduced withholding rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 4 of the International Tax Adjustment Act and Article 51 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, the NTS may disregard the intermediary, reallocate income to the Korean operating entity, and require the arm's length amount plus an additional tax of 40% on the overstated deductions; the use of shell entities to claim a treaty reduction is treated as treaty abuse punishable under Article 12 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and may be referred to the prosecutor's office.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who are signatories to the shell company's bank account and contracts face personal liability when the corporate form is pierced: the tax lien attaches to personal and family assets; in addition to civil restitution, the director may be summoned for investigative interrogation, prohibited from leaving the country under the Immigration Control Act Article 4, and jailed for up to 5 years; de facto directors are held equally liable in administrative audits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Non-Compliance and Illegal Profit Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying an outbound dividend, royalty, or interest to a foreign shareholder without the required 22% Korean withholding, intentionally characterizing a dividend as a tax-deductible service fee or using a Hong Kong intermediary to avoid Korean withholding, or obtaining a DTA reduced rate without a Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership proof.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 98 and Article 111 of the Corporate Tax Act hold the Korean payer jointly liable to remit the unpaid withholding tax, with an additional 10% - 20% surcharge; a false withholding exemption under a tax treaty triggers the 40% erroneous report penalty under Article 47-3 of the Framework Act and, if the unpaid withholding tax exceeds KRW 500 million, criminal prosecution under the Act on Aggravated Punishment of Specific Economic Crimes with imprisonment of more than 3 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorize the remittance without withholding are treated as withholding agents and are personally liable to the National Tax Service for the unremitted amount, interest, and penalties; criminal conviction carries personal imprisonment and a fine equal to 2-5 times the evaded amount; the director may be asset-frozen, default-listed, and deprived of travel rights by the Korea Immigration Service until all restitution is made, including cross-border enforcement through the Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters convention.
